policy: Done means accepted by the developer. A private preview is not a shipped feature. No release dates are promised.

devlog.title: Keeping the prey in sight
devlog.body: Close-range dinosaur tracking and scenery overlap are being refined in the private boss preview.
devlog.changed: Triceratops turns more responsively when the player gets inside its usual attack spacing. Nearby creatures, landmarks and the boss now share a local depth pass.
devlog.testing: Repeated Godot reviews covered turn reversals, both combat phases, attacks, head tracking and corpse handling. A 330-actor stress case passes the current turning check.
devlog.learned: Heading traces showed a physical turning limit at very close range; changing only the visual turning speed was insufficient. Dense tests still expose frame-time spikes.
devlog.next: Continue movement and sound review, optimize dense encounters and preserve frozen-creature effects before developer acceptance.

devlog.title: Keeping busy encounters responsive
devlog.body: The Meteor presentation pass now uses a connected rubble asset and batches the feathered ground-warning geometry. The fight remains in private review.
devlog.changed: Combined dozens of edge draws per warning into one cached mesh while preserving the warning footprint and transparency.
devlog.testing: In one matched local encounter, median frame interval fell from about 30 ms to 9 ms. All nine phase and attack timing samples passed after the change.
devlog.learned: The many small ground-warning draws cost more than expected. Removing model or fire layers did not explain the slowdown.
devlog.next: Review motion, remaining frame spikes, sound and full-fight balance before acceptance.

devlog.title: Attacks that respect terrain
devlog.changed: Dinosaur attacks establish reachable stances; T-rex body and tail share strike progress.
devlog.testing: Actual Godot wall scenarios check body clearance and committed impact alignment. Forward attacks also pass a narrow-corridor check.
devlog.learned: Safe pursuit did not guarantee a safe attack turn. Both need runtime review.
devlog.next: Continue continuous-motion, audio and broader gameplay reviews before developer acceptance.
devlog.body: Private dinosaur attacks now use reachable turn-clear stances. Forward attacks still fit tighter passages, while body and tail motion share strike timing. Focused wall scenarios pass clearance and impact alignment; continuous motion, sound and broader gameplay acceptance remain open. These changes are not in the public playtest.

devlog.title: Contact and surface refinement
devlog.body: The three-boss pass continues with contact, deformation and presentation fixes. These remain private prototypes.
devlog.changed: Dinosaur summon contact now follows the turning torso. Triceratops frill weighting and Meteor fracture surfaces received another refinement pass.
devlog.testing: Actual summon attacks, directional contact and exported attack transitions have been checked in Godot. Encounter reviews also exposed shortcomings in automated dodge planning, which was corrected before drawing balance conclusions.
devlog.learned: Passing geometry and timing checks does not establish finished motion, sound or full-fight balance.
devlog.next: Continue visual and ordinary-build combat reviews, including sound and natural movement, before developer acceptance.

devlog.title: Three bosses, reviewed in the game engine
devlog.body: The current boss pass focuses on T-rex, Triceratops and Meteor. Other bosses wait while these encounters receive animation, interaction and presentation reviews.
devlog.changed: Meteor artwork now has an editable 3D reconstruction. A private rigid-shell motion study has been exported and rendered in Godot; it is not a public gameplay replacement.
devlog.testing: The engine imports one coordinated opening-and-reforming clip with sixteen transform tracks. Runtime renders checked closed and opened states. This verifies portability, not finished art or combat quality.
devlog.learned: Exported motion can work while fracture surfaces still look wrong. A cavity experiment produced broken geometry and was rejected after visual review.
devlog.next: Refine the shell topology, build the combat clips and review the actual encounter. The existing fight deadline remains unchanged. Dinosaur pursuit, attack transitions and sound acceptance remain open.

devlog.title: Triceratops takes its first steps
devlog.body: A dedicated four-legged rig now animates the painted Triceratops reconstruction. The first walk and run clips have been exported and inspected in Godot. Ground contact, turning and attack weight remain under review; this is not yet a public gameplay replacement.
devlog.changed: The original painted reconstruction now has four independent limb chains, a weighted torso and a rigid skull and frill. A slow four-beat walk and a faster diagonal gait are the first motion studies.
devlog.testing: Exported clips were rendered in Godot from four angles. A separate measurement sampled deformed sole vertices through every authored frame; grounded feet stayed at floor height in the current source clips. This does not yet prove turning or runtime contact quality.
devlog.learned: Each creature needs its own anatomy and stance. Reusing the T-rex joint layout would not give a convincing quadruped.
devlog.next: Review skin deformation and moving contact, then build the horn charge, horn sweep and stomp around clear anticipation, impact and recovery.

media.caption: Early Triceratops motion study, rendered in Godot against ground markings. This short silent preview shows two walk cycles; it is not a finished combat animation.

devlog.title: A heavier predator, and a clearer development board
devlog.body: The T-rex motion pass now covers pursuit, turns, bite, rush, tail gust, roar pressure wave and seismic stomp. It remains a development preview awaiting final play review. The remaining boss animation work follows next. Cinematics are accepted as complete; beam prototypes are paused while bosses take priority.
devlog.changed: Longer strides, player-directed head tracking, a continuous tail swing, travelling pressure waves and heavier footfalls now give the T-rex more presence. Promotional comparison footage focuses on creature sound, with character speech removed.
devlog.testing: Matched old and new gameplay captures cover chase, turns and all five attacks. Further live runs checked foot contact, attack direction, pause and death interactions.
devlog.learned: A fixed-frame recording missed a small turning lag seen in a fresh live run. Adding modest visual catch-up capacity corrected it without increasing the physical turn cap.
devlog.next: Complete developer play review before including the rig in a public build. Continue the remaining dinosaur rigs while keeping their progress visible.

media.caption: Development comparison: original sprite fight versus the new T-rex rig. Chase, turns and all five attacks; boss sound without character speech. Final play review is pending.
